approachQuestion.prompt:
Lowest circular reading

A nondecreasing integer array was rotated at an unknown position. Return its minimum value. Duplicates are allowed. The read-only array has random access, 1 <= n <= 200000. Examples: [4,4,1,2,4] -> 1; [7,7] -> 7; [1,0,1,1,1] -> 0. Prefer correctness over an unjustified halving guarantee.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Iterate with lo=0, hi=n-1. If midpoint is below a[hi], set hi=mid; if above, set lo=mid+1; if equal, decrement hi. Return a[lo].
options.feedback: An equal endpoint carries too little information to discard a half; removing one duplicate remains safe.

options.text: Run the same algorithm, first copying the entire array into a new buffer.
options.feedback: The result stays correct but a full copy adds avoidable working storage.

options.text: When midpoint equals a[hi], discard the entire left half including midpoint.
options.feedback: On [1,0,1,1,1], equality at midpoint and right would discard the only minimum.

feedback.reason: Iterate with lo=0, hi=n-1. If midpoint is below a[hi], set hi=mid; if above, set lo=mid+1; if equal, decrement hi. Return a[lo]. An equal endpoint carries too little information to discard a half; removing one duplicate remains safe.
details: Iterate with lo=0, hi=n-1. If midpoint is below a[hi], set hi=mid; if above, set lo=mid+1; if equal, decrement hi. Return a[lo]. An equal endpoint carries too little information to discard a half; removing one duplicate remains safe.

When midpoint equals the right endpoint, either side may contain the minimum. Removing one equal endpoint is safe but may shrink by only one, so duplicates destroy the guaranteed logarithmic worst case.

“Iterate with lo=0, hi=n-1. If midpoint is below a[hi], set hi=mid; if above, set lo=mid+1; if equal, decrement hi. Return a[lo].”: An equal endpoint carries too little information to discard a half; removing one duplicate remains safe.
“Run the same algorithm, first copying the entire array into a new buffer.”: The result stays correct but a full copy adds avoidable working storage.
“When midpoint equals a[hi], discard the entire left half including midpoint.”: On [1,0,1,1,1], equality at midpoint and right would discard the only minimum.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. n is array length. Analyze the iterative method including repeated equal endpoints, with constant-time array access and no copies. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

feedback.reason: Equal-endpoint steps can force a linear scan despite the binary-search structure.
details: For an all-equal array, every midpoint equals the right endpoint, so high decreases by one in each of n-1 iterations. This attains O(n) worst-case time. Only low, high, midpoint, and their values remain live, giving O(1) auxiliary space.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: An equal endpoint carries too little information to discard a half; removing one duplicate remains safe.
“O(n*n + 1) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space”: An equal-endpoint step removes one candidate, so there are at most n such steps, not n², and only scalar bounds are stored.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: An all-equal array can force n-1 endpoint decrements before one candidate remains; constant worst-case time is impossible.
